I found three open JSHack issues labeled `GREENLIGHT`, ordered by issue number:

1. [#156 — Agent skills/content-authoring coverage](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/156) — `GRAVITY-4`
2. [#158 — Hydraulics interaction showcase](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/158) — `GRAVITY-3`
3. [#161 — Monster item-use AI](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/161) — `GRAVITY-2`

[#170](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/170) mentions GREENLIGHT but explicitly says not to add it, so I excluded it.

I feel like these gravity levels should indicate reasoning level --however, my objective has been to take harder issues and push in way more technical details ahead of time to give LUNA a fantastic starting posiition -- so I think they'll all work via LUNA medium.

That makes sense. `GRAVITY-X` should describe the issue’s inherent reasoning and coordination complexity—not prescribe the model.

Your detailed flight plans reduce ambiguity, surface dependencies, and define stop conditions, so even `GRAVITY-4` issues can often start successfully with LUNA medium. A better interpretation is:

- `GRAVITY`: intrinsic complexity and risk
- issue body: required context, constraints, and escalation triggers
- model choice: default to LUNA medium unless the issue’s proof exposes a genuinely harder decision

That makes the tags useful for prioritization without artificially routing well-prepared work to a heavier model.
I don't know if it's time for the skills work --- scan the issues list, lets find better next issue(s) to work on.

content.text:
After scanning the open list, I agree that #156 is probably not the best next move. It improves the machinery for future agents, but it doesn’t create a player-facing win.

My strongest candidates are:

1. [#158 — Hydraulics showcase](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/158) — best immediate implementation. It is bounded, uses existing mechanics, and produces a concrete discovery moment. `GRAVITY-3`, but the issue already supplies strong technical scaffolding for LUNA medium.

2. [#161 — Monster item-use AI](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/161) — smallest, safest player-facing slice. It validates existing AI behavior, canonical item transfer, and tactical counterplay. `GRAVITY-2`.

3. [#157 — Mechanic surfacing audit](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/157) — best if we want evidence before committing. It can quickly identify which existing mechanic has the highest payoff and prevent us from building a showcase around something unreachable or silent.

I’d defer these for now:

- [#170 — World exploration](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/170): excellent direction, but a large coordination umbrella.
- [#171 — Leveling](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/171): compelling, but introduces a new persistent progression contract.
- [#163 — Corpse adaptations](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/163): valuable, but has a substantial discovery/persistence/UI surface.
- [#166 — Town contracts](https://github.com/PJensen/JSHack/issues/166): economy-to-quest coupling makes it riskier.
- [#172 — Stat scaling research](https://github.com/PJensen/JSHack/issues/172): useful research, but not the next player-visible improvement.
- [#159 — Discovery-first pattern](https://github.com/PJensen/JSHack/issues/159): explicitly wants #158 proven first.

My suggested sequence is:

`#157 audit → #158 hydraulics slice → #161 AI slice → #159 pattern extraction`

If we want to start implementing immediately, I’d pick #158.
I just felt like skills would HELP with continued development.

Yes—that’s a good instinct. Skills work is infrastructure for making every subsequent issue faster and safer, especially with LUNA medium.

My concern is only that #156’s full scope is too broad as the immediate task. A better approach would be:

- Work on a concrete issue such as #158 or #161.
- Capture the real authoring path, test workflow, and common pitfalls.
- Make a focused update to the relevant skill afterward.
- Expand toward #156 incrementally as patterns are proven.

That gives us immediate gameplay progress while turning each completed issue into better guidance for continued development.
it's almost like we want to updated AGENTS.md to perform skill capture as we're going -- incrementally

Exactly. Rather than treating #156 as one large documentation project, `AGENTS.md` could make skill capture part of the normal delivery loop:

1. Before work: identify whether the issue exposes a reusable workflow.
2. During work: record canonical files, commands, invariants, and failure modes.
3. After work: update or create the smallest relevant skill.
4. Validate the skill against the completed implementation.
5. Keep broad coverage work incremental and evidence-based.

The key rule would be: capture proven practice, not speculative architecture.

That turns every gameplay issue into two outputs:

- the feature itself;
- a better starting point for the next LUNA session.

It also makes #156 a rolling objective rather than a prerequisite gate.
Approving this pre-GREENLIGHT work item, there are many buried tools, processes and best practices all over this project.

I’ll turn that approval into a focused `AGENTS.md` rule: capture reusable tools, processes, and best practices incrementally as each issue is implemented, without making the broad skills audit a prerequisite.
